notes: Hand-verified against the scenario's own arithmetic before comparing to reference-model output. Partner C contributes $60,000.00 cash; Partner D contributes equipment at its $60,000.00 fair market value (book depreciation: $60,000.00 / 60 months = $1,000.00/month exactly, the same as FA-001's identical cost/life). Every month: revenue 3000.00, expense 1000.00, depreciation 1000.00, net income 1000.00 — flat every month, since there is no disposal or other one-time event.

Cash is only affected by revenue and the cash expense (depreciation is non-cash, and D's contribution was never cash in the first place): cash change = 3000.00 − 1000.00 = 2000.00/month. Cumulative cash through month M: 60000.00 (C's opening contribution) + 2000.00×M.

2026-01 (M=1): cash = 60000.00 + 2000.00 = 62000.00. accumulated_depreciation_equipment = −1000.00. Balance sheet: assets (cash 62000.00 + equipment 60000.00 − 1000.00) 121000.00 = equity (partner_c_capital 60000.00 + partner_d_capital 60000.00 + current_period_earnings 1000.00) 121000.00.

2026-12 (December alone, after the first 50/50 closing): December's own net income is the same 1000.00 as every month. Full year 2026 net income 12000.00 (12×1000.00), split 6000.00/6000.00 — partner_c_capital = 60000.00 + 6000.00 = 66000.00, same for D. Cash at M=12: 60000.00 + 24000.00 = 84000.00.

2028-06 (M=30, mid-run): cash = 60000.00 + 60000.00 = 120000.00. accumulated_depreciation_equipment = −30000.00 (half the asset's life). Cumulative closed income through the 2026 and 2027 closings (12000.00×2 = 24000.00) split 12000.00/12000.00, plus each partner's 60000.00 starting capital: partner_c_capital = partner_d_capital = 72000.00 at the start of 2028. current_period_earnings (Jan–Jun 2028) = 6×1000.00 = 6000.00. Balance sheet: assets (cash 120000.00 + equipment 60000.00 − 30000.00) 150000.00 = equity (72000.00×2 + 6000.00) 150000.00.

2030-01 (M=49): cash = 60000.00 + 98000.00 = 158000.00. accumulated_depreciation_equipment = −49000.00. Cumulative closed income through 2026–2029 (12000.00×4 = 48000.00) split 24000.00/24000.00, plus 60000.00 starting capital: partner_c_capital = 84000.00.

2030-12 (M=60, the asset's final depreciation month, after the fifth and final closing): accumulated_depreciation_equipment reaches exactly −60000.00 — the equipment is now fully depreciated, net book value 60000.00 − 60000.00 = 0.00. Cash = 60000.00 + 120000.00 = 180000.00. Cumulative closed income across all five years (12000.00×5 = 60000.00) split 30000.00/30000.00, plus 60000.00 starting capital: final partner_c_capital = partner_d_capital = 90000.00. Balance sheet: assets (cash 180000.00, equipment fully depreciated) 180000.00 = equity (90000.00 + 90000.00) 180000.00 exactly.

2026/2028/2030 (full fiscal years, identical to each other): revenue 36000.00, expense 12000.00, depreciation 12000.00, net income 12000.00. 2026's cash flow includes the one-time contribution/purchase activity (operating_cash_flow 144000.00 = net_income 12000.00 + accumulated_depreciation +12000.00 (the depreciation add-back) + partner_c_capital +60000.00 + partner_d_capital +60000.00 (C's cash contribution and D's non-cash equipment contribution, both equity increases); investing_cash_flow −60000.00 for the equipment; total 84000.00 = ending_cash 84000.00 − beginning_cash 0.00). 2028 and 2030 have no contribution/purchase activity (operating_cash_flow 24000.00 = 12000.00 + 12000.00, matching their own 24000.00 cash change).

Section 704(c) built-in gain allocation (not posted to this ledger): see docs/accounting-policy.md and tests/integration/test_part_003_section_704c.py. Book depreciation (1000.00/month) is split 50/50 for GAAP purposes (as reflected in net income above); the asset's tax basis is $30,000.00, giving $500.00/month of total tax depreciation (30000.00 / 60 months) and a $30,000.00 built-in gain (60000.00 FMV − 30000.00 tax basis). Under the traditional method's ceiling rule, Partner C's (the non-contributing partner's) book share of depreciation (500.00/month) exactly consumes all $500.00/month of available tax depreciation, leaving Partner D (the contributing partner) with $0.00/month of tax depreciation for the asset's entire 60-month life — the well-known 'ceiling rule problem.'
